$comment: HELMION RULE MANIFEST. Every rule the operator has written down, with an honest
statement of whether a machine can enforce it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Before it, the rules lived in one markdown file that only
the model read. An audit on 2026-07-30 found 25 rules and TWO with any code
behind them; every rule about HONESTY had none. That is backwards for a product
whose whole premise is that a session can drift and no session can tell. The
rules have to be DATA that ships, not prose one tool happens to load.
THE THREE CLASSES ARE THE POINT. A manifest claiming all 26 are enforced would
be the exact failure this is meant to stop, so each rule declares which it is:
gate       a hook observes it and blocks or flags it. Real enforcement.
observable a hook can see the evidence AFTER the fact and record a breach,
but cannot prevent it. Makes drift visible.
judgment   no hook can decide it without either firing constantly or never.
Named honestly here so nobody wonders why it has no gate.
'gate' entries name the script that enforces them. 'installed: false' means the
script exists and is proven but is not registered in a settings file yet.

rules.title: Honesty overrides everything
rules.note: The parent rule. Enforced in practice by 0.001, 0.002 and 0.16, which are its checkable parts.

rules.title: Source of truth and full tracing
rules.note: A hook can see whether a file was READ before a claim was made about it, because the read is a tool call.

rules.title: Cite or shut up
rules.note: Flags hedging with no evidence. Passes a sentence carrying file:line, an exit code, a measured number, a URL, or an explicit UNVERIFIED stamp. Proven both directions 2026-07-30.

rules.title: Parallel by default
rules.note: Countable: independent tool calls issued one per turn instead of batched.

rules.title: Voice reads everything in the reply
Voice must be short
rules.note: RETIRED 2026-07-30 by the operator. Being made to wait between short clips was worse for him than one long clip. Do not reinstate a word cap.

rules.title: Voice mode protocol
rules.note: Same rule as 0.19. Needs a marker written when the notification fires; a gate that reads a marker nothing writes is unsatisfiable.

rules.title: Post-push visual ping
rules.note: A push is a visible tool call, so requiring the ping after it is decidable.

rules.title: Done means verified end to end
rules.note: Shares the 0.002 gate: 'done', 'fixed' and 'works' are claims, and the gate asks for the evidence.

rules.title: Never remove the operator's ability to stop
rules.note: Already live on the operator's machine: submitting anything writes a STOP sentinel and kills playback.

rules.title: Advisory lane writes only to the low-trust table
Every session records its failures and successes
A lesson names a number and a file:line
rules.note: Decidable: a lesson entry either contains a citation and a number or it does not.

rules.title: Verified auto-push with an escape hatch
rules.note: Live and repeatedly effective: it blocked two commits on 2026-07-30, once for missing QA evidence and once for undeclared file deletions.

rules.title: Never make the operator do what the agent can do
rules.note: Requires knowing what the agent COULD have done, which is the thing in question.

rules.title: Never change the plan without saying so

destructive_gates.$comment: Already live and proven. These are why the honesty gap stood out: the rules that stop damage had teeth, the rules that stop lying had none.

hooks.blocks: rm -rf, Remove-Item -Recurse, git reset --hard, git clean -f, force push, DROP, TRUNCATE, dd, mkfs
schema changes, auth surfaces, production database writes, cross-project edits
